source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Free-water loss with hypernatremia and persistently dilute urine.","B":"Isotonic volume depletion with hypernatremia and maximally concentrated urine from appropriate vasopressin release.","C":"Water retention with hypotonic hyponatremia and urine that remains inappropriately concentrated.","D":"Hypertonic hyponatremia with maximally dilute urine caused by complete suppression of vasopressin."}}
source_row.rationale: In SIAD, inappropriate vasopressin activity increases renal water reabsorption, producing water retention, dilutional hypotonic hyponatremia, and urine that is not maximally dilute. This contrasts with diabetes insipidus, which causes free-water loss and dilute urine.
